title: Repentance and Self-Knowledge
english: The synagogue, in repentance, turns towards Christ. It is imperative that you reveal yourself to me, so that I, who shepherd your churches, may remain with the veil on my heart. If you do not possess self-knowledge, you will be found lagging behind the nations, devoid of the fruits of righteousness and unfruitful. I have compared you to my horse, for you have received my faith and have been likened to the apostles. Your charioteers were prepared to face the spiritual Pharaoh, and your reins are like a vine, for the reins of a vine are red.

However, the synagogue has been given the face of a prostitute, shameless before all. The submissive neck of the soul bears the yoke of Christ, for silver usually represents divine teaching, while gold represents divine gifts. Before Christ's coming, all things were mere likenesses and shadows of what was to come, according to the Apostle. But with Christ's resurrection, perfect things have been given to humanity, and the Church, having received His faith, has been likened to the apostles.

The bride is declared to be good, and this praise is not limited to her being among women, but now she is also near to the bridegroom, who doubles his praise of her, acknowledging both her theoretical and practical virtues. He notes that her eyes are turned towards the mind and heart, and, like a dove, she possesses discerning qualities, which are also characteristic of the Spirit.

The bridegroom's praise of the bride is not merely superficial, but rather it is a deep and abiding appreciation for her inner qualities, which have been awakened and are now being expressed, for he says that she has received mind, and this is evident in her thoughts and actions. As it is written, 'You shall ride upon your horses, and your cavalry shall be salvation' (Full Book, no specific reference given).

title: The Bride and the Archer
english: Seeing God alone, the Church's teachers are both the pure and the sharp-sighted. I am the flower of the field. The Church, as the bride of Christ, receives the heavenly rain and gives birth to virtue, and in doing so, she shows how much Christ's presence has benefited her, even transforming the valleys, for he says the valleys are those that were once inhabited by demons.

The Church's teachers are pure and sharp-sighted, and they secure us with the words of the Gospel, which make Christ sweet to us. I want to be counted among the saints, for they are like apples, and the law is on the left, while the Gospel is on the right, guiding us towards eternal life. The right hand represents the knowledge of divine things, from which comes eternal life, while the left hand represents human knowledge, from which comes wealth and glory.

As the bride is taken into the participation of imperishable eternity, she receives the gift of length of life and years of life, bestowed through the right hand. This participation is a sharing in the eternal nature of God, which is characterized by imperishable eternity.

In contrast, those who seek the glory of the world are deprived of the wealth of eternal goods and the glory of God, which are given through the left hand. The speaker notes that the Euonymus of God is upon their head, through which…

title: The Soul's Union with the Divine Through Hands of Action
english: It is directed toward the mark, the arrow; his right hand has taken me and drawn me back, producing a light upward motion.
There, sent forth and not parted from the archer, it finds its rest rather than continuing onward.
Then he turns his speech toward the daughters of the heavenly Jerusalem.

His word is consolation, brought forward under oath, designed to increase and augment love without cease, until he makes his will effective—the will of the one who desires all people to be saved and to arrive at the knowledge of truth.
Through the left hand, he signifies the good things of this present life, which he already enjoys, as it seems.
Through the right hand, he points to the expectation of future blessings held in promise, and he says he attaches himself to the use of these things in promises and in hopes, as has been said.
Well also to say: to be embraced by the right hand, and to let the head rest upon the left.

For it is necessary that even if the things of this present life are considered good and beautiful, they be subordinated to the head of the perfect soul, supplying only the body’s necessary need, like the forecranium to the head.
But the things of the age to come, since they are divine and rise above human nature, have been signified as surpassing through comprehension.
Perhaps, because the hands are symbols of action: the actions of the left hand indicate bodily matters, and those of the right hand, spiritual things.
The right hand has obtained the better portion, and thus contains the bodily necessities.

Just as the hand that embraces holds its treasure safely within the close ring of arms, so too the deeds set apart for the aim of the life to come gather every disordered impulse of the body into a harmonious unity, guarding the soul in right order and indissoluble bond.
No enemy can find a breach to assail that soul which the bridegroom has clasped to himself.
